display_name: Penfolds Bin 2 Mataro, South Eastern Australia
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Mataro (the Australian name for Monastrell) rarely leads a commercial Australian blend, but Penfolds built Bin 2 around its high-acid, rustic structure to anchor Syrah’s plush fruit.",
  "wine_summary": "Penfolds operates on a multi-regional blending model that prioritizes house style over single-vineyard transparency. Bin 2 pulls fruit from McLaren Vale’s warmer inland sites and cooler coastal blocks, balancing ripe blackberry and plum against Monastrell’s dried herb and earthy backbone. The 14.5% ABV across the 2007–2013 run reflects a warm period in South Australia, where extended sun hours pushed sugar accumulation while the Gulf St Vincent sea breeze preserved enough acidity to prevent flabbiness. You get a wine built for early drinking but structured enough to handle rich proteins.",
  "terroir_expression": "McLaren Vale’s red-brown earths and dark cracking clay retain heat and hold moisture deep into dry summers, forcing Syrah and Monastrell roots downward for concentrated fruit. The 50 to 350-meter elevation range creates temperature swings that lock in phenolic ripeness before sugar spikes. These soils translate directly to the glass: the clay delivers dense, plush mid-palate weight, while the iron-rich red-brown earths contribute a subtle ferrous minerality and dried leaf character that cuts through the jammy fruit.",
  "vinification_summary": "American oak aging anchors the flavor architecture, but the real structural work happens during fermentation. The winemaking team uses punch-down cap management, a process of physically pushing grape skins back into the fermenting juice to extract color and tannin without pulling excessive bitterness from the seeds. Seasoned American hogsheads contribute vanillin and lactones that soften Monastrell’s naturally grippy texture, while a short 12-month barrique period keeps primary fruit forward and prevents heavy wood masking.",
  "food_pairing": "The high alcohol and structured tannins make this a natural partner for fatty, heavily seasoned proteins. Nashville hot chicken works because the 14.5% alcohol and firm tannins slice through fried fat, while the wine’s black pepper notes mirror the cayenne heat without amplifying burn. Braised lamb shoulder with rosemary and black olive gremolata aligns directly with Monastrell’s savory, olive-tinged profile, and the wine’s earthy depth matches slow-cooked collagen. Smoked brisket with whole-grain mustard barbecue sauce lets the mustard’s acidity lift the dense mid-palate, while smoke compounds bind with the American oak vanillin and Syrah’s meaty rotundone character.",
  "comparable_wines": [
    "d’Arenberg The Dead Arm Shiraz — shares McLaren Vale’s clay-driven concentration and warm-climate fruit weight, though it leans heavier on single-varietal power rather than Mataro’s structural tension.",
    "Yalumba Y Series Shiraz — matches the accessible price tier and American oak treatment, but trades the earthy grip for brighter cherry notes and a softer finish."
  ],
  "style_profile": "Medium-to-full-bodied dry red with plush dark fruit, firm tannic grip, and earthy, meaty undertones.",
  "cellar_recommendation": "The 2007 through 2013 vintages have passed their peak and should be opened within weeks of purchase. Current releases drink best within three to six years, stored horizontally at 12–14°C with moderate humidity.",
  "value_assessment": "$20 to $30 retail places this against Yalumba Y Series Shiraz and Wolf Blass Yellow Label Cabernet Shiraz, both of which offer similar drinkability. Bin 2 wins on structural backbone and savory complexity, making it a better buy for meat-heavy meals than the softer, fruit-driven competitors.",
  "market_position": "Beverage directors stock Bin 2 for mid-tier restaurant programs and corporate events where consistent, crowd-pleasing reds are required. Retail buyers pick it up for reliable weeknight drinking, while casual collectors view it as an entry point to the Penfolds house style before moving up to Bin 28 or 389.",
  "insider_take": "Skip this if you expect primary fruit purity or vineyard-specific transparency. Bin 2 is a structural exercise built for savory food and early drinking, and chasing older vintages will only yield flat, oxidized bottles.",
  "aging_potential_years": 6,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 0,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 6,
